svg.aria-label: Master plan of Zero Mile International: six east-west runways in two triples, the seven-lobed Zero Mile Hall to the west with three gateway lobes pointing at Ahmedabad, Mumbai and Bengaluru, one continuous roof over the Hall, the Mall and twelve piers, remote stands, cargo and maintenance to the east, and phase 2 satellites shown dashed.
svg.text: seven lobes; three gateways point home
PHASE 2 · REMOTE STANDS AT THE PIER TIPS
PHASE 2 · REMOTE STANDS AT THE PIER TIPS
TRANSFER: INTERNATIONAL TO DOMESTIC, ABOUT 25 MIN
Arrive at an F north stand, walk to the Mall, clear the transfer centre (T) at the D/E junction:
immigration and re-screening. Then the APM to B and a short walk to a B south stand.
Mumbai–Nagpur high-speed rail (proposed), in tunnel under the field
Metro spur to the Orange Line
Master plan · 6 runways · 304 stands (168 contact + 136 remote) · 56 MARS · up to 360 aircraft parked · 6 holding bays
One continuous roof: Hall, Mall, 12 piers (phase 1)
Phase 2: satellites G and H, pier-tip remote aprons
People mover to G and H (phase 2)
MARS stand: one widebody or two narrowbodies
Gateway axis: from the oculus toward home
Transfer journey, F north to B south
Stepwell forecourt under the 40 m cantilever
The three gateway axes meet under the oculus, at the Zero
Mile marker. Mumbai builds the roof, Bengaluru plants its
Outer parallels run west. In the midfield the runway-side
parallel runs west and the terminal-side parallel runs
east. The end-arounds mean no runway crossings.
Contact: 168 stands, 40 of them MARS. Remote: 136 stands,
16 MARS. A MARS stand takes one widebody or two
narrowbodies, so up to 360 aircraft can park at once. Plus
satellites, G and H, replace the east remote rows; remote
stands move to the pier-tip aprons.
